message.content:
### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| **1** | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| **2** | **Gather Parts** | All components must fit together. | Check compatibility lists (e.g., CPU socket vs. motherboard). |
| **3** | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Use an anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| **4** | **Open the Case** | Access internal space. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| **5** | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all parts. | Mount it with screws, route cables to the back. |
| **6** | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for everything else. | Align standoffs, screw in, then connect the 24‑pin ATX and 8‑pin EPS cables. |
| **7** | **Install the CPU** | Core of your system. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock. |
| **8** | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Prevent overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount; choose air or liquid cooler based on case clearance. |
| **9** | **Insert RAM** | Memory for multitasking. | Snap sticks into matching slots; refer to motherboard manual for dual‑channel layout. |
| **10** | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into the M.2 slot; for SATA drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
| **11** | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Visual performance. | Slide into the top PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect 6/8‑pin power if needed. |
| **12** | **Connect All Cables** | Power and data flow. | SATA data cables, power connectors, front‑panel headers (USB, audio, power button). |
| **13** | **Cable Management** | Airflow & aesthetics. | Tuck cables behind the motherboard tray, use zip ties. |
| **14** | **Double‑Check Connections** | Avoid shorts or missing power. | Verify all screws, cables, and component seating. |
| **15** | **Close the Case** | Protect components. | Reattach side panels, secure with screws. |
| **16** | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Confirm hardware detection. | Power on, enter BIOS (usually **Del** or **F2**), set boot order, enable XMP for RAM. |
| **17** | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Turn your PC into a usable machine. | Use a USB installer (Windows, Linux, etc.), follow on‑screen prompts. |
| **18** | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works optimally. | Download latest GPU, chipset, and peripheral drivers. |
| **19** | **Test & Benchmark** | Verify stability and performance. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark) and monitor temperatures. |
| **20** | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep your PC running smoothly. | Clean dust filters, update firmware, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU + Cooler** ✔️
- **Motherboard + Standoffs** ✔️
- **RAM** ✔️
- **Storage (M.2 / SATA)** ✔️
- **GPU** ✔️
- **PSU** ✔️
- **Case** ✔️
- **Cables (SATA, power, front panel)** ✔️
- **Anti‑static precautions** ✔️

#### Common Pitfalls & Fixes

| Issue | Likely Cause | Fix |
|-------|--------------|-----|
| PC doesn’t power on | PSU not connected or faulty | Check PSU switch, cables, try a known‑good PSU |
| No display | GPU not seated or wrong power connector | Re‑seat GPU, ensure power cable is plugged |
| Overheating | Poor airflow or insufficient cooling | Add case fans, reapply thermal paste |
| Random restarts | Power supply under‑rated | Upgrade PSU to higher wattage |
| BIOS not detecting GPU | Wrong PCI‑e slot or BIOS setting | Move GPU to primary slot, enable “PCI‑e x16” in BIOS |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – *Linus Tech Tips*, *JayzTwoCents*, *Paul’s Hardware* for visual guides.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals for specific instructions.

Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
